---
title: "Competitive Mapping"
---

# How it works

Minimap2 maps reads against a “manifest” which is simply a multifasta of target sequences. The targets can then be ordered by mean depth (average number of reads mapping to each site in the genome) and coverage (proportion of genome which has at least 1 read mapping to it), allowing top hits to be reported.

- In Myco the manifest is a collection of reference genomes for Mycobacterial species

To calculate the summary stats (mean depth, coverage etc) there are two methods in use:

- `samtools coverage`and some python scripts. This is used by Myco at the moment

## Note on Myco

Where the number of reads mapped to *M. tuberculosis* meets a threshold (which is different for Illumina and ONT), the sample has enough reads to progress to genome assembly. This should happen even if *M. tuberculosis* is not the “top hit”. The TB always has priority in the portal, and will be displayed in the batch view even if the NTM has higher mean depth or coverage.

# Thresholds

See code for all details. Main thing to be aware of:

- results are ordered by mean depth.
- `-N 1000` is used with minimap2 to get up to 1000 secondary alignments. 1000 is just a big number so as to catch all alignments
- `-x sr` and `-x map-ont` are used to use default minimap2 settings

## Samtools coverage

The samtools coverage approach produces an output json like the following. 

- primary reads are reads where it’s best alignment is to that target
- secondary reads mean the read maps better to a different target
- exclusive reads mean that the read maps only to that target (these are a subset of primary reads)
- supplementary read is when half of the read maps to one place, and half to another. Feel free to ignore

## Tie Break

This works in two rounds:

- In the first round only high quality alignments to single targets are used. The references are then ordered by genome coverage
- In the second round more alignments are allowed, and when ties occur the genome ordering from round 1 is used to tie break

The result is that each read ends up mapped to a single reference. The output is a csv.

The params for this process are specified [here](https://github.com/GlobalPathogenAnalysisService/competitivemapping_pipeline/blob/main/process/params_illumina.yml).

### Ani groups

the mapping approach works significantly less well with very closely related targets. Hence “ani groups” (ANI=average nucleotide identity) are used. References in the same group are treated like a single reference, so reads can only map to one group, but within a group a read can map to many reference.

### Example output

There are more rows with depth-type “unique”, “winner” etc but these can be ignored. Likewise the columns starting “robust”.

- median\_nonzero\_depth is the median depth of all sites which have depth\>0
- simple\_expected\_coverage is an estimate of expected coverage based on the mean\_depth. It is based on a poisson distribution.
